articles.headline: Adai define una «paisaxe sagrada» con 5.000 años de rituales
articles.subtitle: La USC excava hasta el viernes el entorno del Corro dos Mouros, un recinto circular usado durante un milenio, y sitúa ceremonias allí desde el cuarto milenio antes de Cristo.
articles.body:
La arqueóloga de la USC Pilar Prieto define el entorno del Corro dos Mouros, en la parroquia de Adai, a ocho kilómetros de Lugo, como «unha paisaxe sagrada para distintas cerimonias». La campaña de excavación abierta a principios de mes busca precisamente datar ese uso continuado, y se cerrará el próximo viernes.

El recinto circular, de 52 metros de diámetro, estuvo en uso durante un milenio, entre los siglos XIII y III antes de Cristo. Las tres campañas desarrolladas desde 2023 han dejado 5.000 piezas, unas 330 muestras y 14 dataciones, que sitúan rituales en Penas do Caldeiro desde el cuarto milenio antes de Cristo —cuando se levantaron al menos siete mámoas— hasta la construcción de la «roda», ya en el Bronce Final.

## La cabaña de Pena Fita

Los trabajos se centran ahora en el Altar de Adai, conocido como Pena Fita: una piedra de unos 40 metros cuadrados con agujeros que imitarían la planta de un barco. La hipótesis del equipo es que se trata de una «longhouse», una cabaña grande de uso comunal, y que los orificios sostenían los postes.

Las cerámicas halladas allí se parecen a las del Corro dos Mouros y a las del castro de Penarrubia, a medio kilómetro, lo que relaciona los tres lugares.

Los arqueólogos han abierto además dos sondeos en abrigos del terreno, uno de ellos en Pena Travesa, y confían en llegar al fondo antes de que acabe la campaña. La investigación continuará con el Proyecto Rodas, de cuatro años y financiado por el Ministerio de Cultura, que estudiará el paisaje y el clima del entorno para reconstruir cómo se usó el yacimiento.

La USC ha programado una visita abierta al público el jueves 17, a las 17.00 horas, guiada por Prieto y con salida desde el dolmen de Adai.

articles.headline: Lugo convertirá en glorieta física la rotonda «fantasma» de Ramón Ferreiro
articles.subtitle: El Concello tendrá listo en octubre el proyecto de una intersección hoy señalizada solo con pintura sobre el asfalto, y sumará aparcamientos en la zona.
articles.body:
El Concello de Lugo sustituirá por una glorieta física el cruce de Ramón Ferreiro y Rodríguez Mourelo con Vilalba y Alcalde Anxo López Pérez, hoy señalizado solo con marcas viales sobre el asfalto. El proyecto de ejecución de los primeros trabajos estará listo en octubre, según el gobierno local, que enmarca la actuación en una revisión global del viario de la zona.

El ámbito abarca las calles Salvador de Madariaga, Dinán, Senador Xacinto Calvo, Galicia y Celso Emilio Ferreiro, además de la Praza da Bretaña. Celso Emilio Ferreiro y un tramo de la plaza pasarán a ser de doble sentido, un cambio que el Concello justifica por las necesidades de los vehículos de la Guardia Civil.

## Los otros cruces señalados

La obra incluye medidas para el peatón, como ampliar la acera entre Vilalba y Bispo Aguirre, y el estudio de alternativas para ganar plazas de aparcamiento entre Pintor Corredoira y Fonte do Rei, junto a la Horta do Seminario.

Con el reinicio del curso escolar vuelven a aflorar otros puntos complejos. El cruce de Ángelo Colocci con Santo Grial, en A Piringalla, próximo a centros escolares, es el que más quejas vecinales acumula. También generan riesgo el enlace de Avenida da Coruña con Curros Enríquez y García Abad, por el giro de los autobuses, y el de San Roque con Marina Española y Pena do Rei, sin semáforos y con visibilidad escasa.

En O Ceao, el Concello inició la noche del domingo la repavimentación de la rotonda que une Benigno Rivera con Infanta Elena, un cruce que se inunda con las lluvias torrenciales. Los trabajos se harán hasta el miércoles entre las 22.30 y las 07.00 horas para reducir el impacto en el tráfico.

articles.headline: El Gobierno cifra en 2.100 los menores migrantes en Ceuta y reclama su traslado
articles.subtitle: Sira Rego pide «responsabilidad» a las comunidades y el PP responde que la dimisión del jefe de Gabinete de la Delegación demuestra que el Ejecutivo «miente».
articles.body:
La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, cifró este sábado en unos 2.100 los menores migrantes ya filiados en el sistema de acogida de Ceuta —700 de ellos niñas— y reclamó a las comunidades autónomas que asuman su traslado a la Península para aliviar la ciudad autónoma.

«Es imposible que un territorio tan pequeño como Ceuta en un evento de esta magnitud pueda hacerse cargo de todo esto», dijo Rego en declaraciones en Córdoba, donde apeló a la «responsabilidad política» de las autonomías y recordó que la tutela de los menores en situación de desamparo corresponde por ley a las comunidades. Aún quedan niños por filiar y se ha desplazado una unidad multidisciplinar para agilizar las entrevistas, que deben ser individualizadas.

El Gobierno ha iniciado además los expedientes de los menores que han manifestado que quieren volver con sus familias a Marruecos. Se remitirán «con carácter urgente», aunque el procedimiento requiere comprobar que existe una estructura familiar en el país de origen. Rego subrayó que muchos de estos niños huyen de situaciones extremas, incluidos casos de niñas que escapan de violencia sexual o de matrimonios forzosos.

## La respuesta del PP

El portavoz nacional del PP, Borja Sémper, calificó de «broma» que la única responsabilidad política asumida sea la dimisión del jefe de Gabinete de la Delegación del Gobierno en Ceuta, Gonzalo Sanz, y acusó al Ejecutivo de «mentir» a los españoles y de actuar con «soberbia». Sémper advirtió a Marruecos de que «con España no se juega» y pidió a Pedro Sánchez que disuelva las Cortes.

El presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, sostuvo que «la agresión de Marruecos continúa» y que «Ceuta será el epitafio de Sánchez», pidió a los socios del PSOE que precipiten el final de la legislatura y reclamó que Ceuta, Melilla y Canarias «no pueden estar en cuestión».

articles.headline: Bolaños pide al Supremo que resuelva el voto de los nacionalizados antes de 2027
articles.subtitle: El ministro considera «muy discutible jurídicamente» el auto que suspende el voto de los beneficiarios de la ley de nietos, en línea con jueces y fiscales progresistas.
articles.body:
El ministro de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, Félix Bolaños, pidió este sábado «respetuosamente» al Tribunal Supremo que resuelva sobre el derecho al voto de los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos antes de las elecciones de 2027, y calificó de «muy discutible jurídicamente» el auto que lo suspende de forma cautelar.

El Supremo acordó suspender los efectos electorales de la inscripción en el Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) de quienes obtuvieron la nacionalidad por la Ley de Memoria Democrática sin acreditar que descienden de exiliados. Los magistrados apreciaron un «peligro fundado, real y serio» de que el incremento extraordinario del censo —408.262 electores desde las generales de 2023— afecte a la objetividad y la transparencia del proceso electoral.

La medida responde a los recursos de Vox y de la plataforma Iustitia Europa, que acusaron al Gobierno de inflar el censo con intención partidista. No afecta a las concesiones de nacionalidad, aprobadas o en curso, pero quienes ya estaban inscritos solo podrán votar si los responsables de los registros consulares certifican su condición de hijos o nietos de exiliados.

Bolaños se hizo eco del comunicado de Jueces y Juezas para la Democracia y de la Unión Progresista de Fiscales, que consideran desproporcionada la decisión, y sostuvo que «el censo no puede alterarse sin base legal sólida». El ministro advirtió además de que el fallo está generando «interpretaciones diversas y algún tipo de confusión».

Según los últimos datos oficiales, 2,4 millones de descendientes de quienes se exiliaron por la Guerra Civil o la dictadura han solicitado la nacionalidad por esta vía, 544.722 la tienen ya aprobada y unos 306.000 están inscritos como españoles.

articles.headline: Miles de personas se concentran en Oviedo contra la agresión a dos activistas
articles.subtitle: Los médicos Rubén Rosón y Jorge Fernández, agredidos en la madrugada del viernes en San Mateo, piden que «el fascismo no sea bienvenido» en Asturias.
articles.body:
Miles de personas, 5.000 según los convocantes, llenaron este sábado la plaza de la Catedral de Oviedo para rechazar la agresión sufrida dos días antes por el exconcejal de Somos Oviedo Rubén Rosón y el médico Jorge Fernández, ambos vinculados a AMA Asturies y al colectivo Fiestes Populares.

El ataque se produjo pasadas las tres de la madrugada del viernes, en la primera noche de las fiestas de San Mateo. Según el relato de las víctimas, un grupo de unos ocho jóvenes arrancó la bandera arcoíris y un cartel antirracista de la caseta en la que colaboraban y les golpeó con puñetazos y patadas cuando les recriminaron los destrozos, entre insultos como «maricones» y «rojos de mierda» y gritos de «Arriba España» al marcharse.

Ambos fueron atendidos en el Hospital Universitario Central de Asturias. Rosón necesitó cinco puntos de sutura y Fernández recibió impactos en la cabeza; los dos recibieron el alta y han denunciado los hechos ante la Policía Nacional, que analiza las grabaciones para identificar a los agresores.

## «Asturias es una región de acogida»

«El fascismo no es bienvenido en nuestra tierra, Asturias es una región de acogida», proclamó Rosón ante una plaza en la que también estuvieron el coordinador federal de IU, Antonio Maíllo, y el exdirigente Gaspar Llamazares. No se registraron incidentes durante la protesta; al término de la concentración, parte de los asistentes marchó hacia el Campo de San Francisco.

La agresión generó una oleada de condenas del Principado, partidos, sindicatos y organizaciones sociales. El presidente asturiano, Adrián Barbón, reclamó que caiga «todo el peso de la ley» sobre los responsables, y la Delegación del Gobierno autorizó la marcha pese al informe desfavorable de la Policía Local.

articles.headline: Trump says he would «love to see» a united Ireland and triggers unionist backlash
articles.subtitle: The US president said Irish unification is «going to happen eventually» and would be «cool», prompting the DUP, TUV and UUP to insist that Northern Ireland's future will be decided by its own people.
articles.body:
Donald Trump said he would «love to see» a united Ireland during his two-day visit to the Republic, telling reporters alongside the Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, that it was «going to happen eventually, it may as well happen now». Later, at the US ambassador's residence in Dublin, he returned to the theme: «To be honest with you, I think it would be cool.»

The remarks landed in the middle of a visit dominated until then by security, protests and golf. Trump was asked for his view during a call with President Catherine Connolly, before heading to the Irish Open at his Doonbeg course in Co Clare, where his sons Eric and Donald Jr are expected to join him.

Unionist leaders pushed back within hours. DUP leader Gavin Robinson posted on X that «Northern Ireland's constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington», adding that unionists «are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish Republic».

TUV leader Jim Allister said Trump «is not the first US president to meddle in the affairs which don't concern him», insisting the North is «not a pawn in Trump's fall-out with the UK». UUP leader Jon Burrows said the president was entitled to his view, but «the only people whose decision counts are the people of Northern Ireland» — the principle of consent «now enshrined in law through the Belfast Agreement».

Trump's former special envoy to Northern Ireland, Mick Mulvaney, cautioned against reading too much into the comments. «This does not represent a shift in US foreign policy,» he told the BBC. «We're still very much committed to the Good Friday Agreement.» Democratic congressman Brendan Boyle agreed that bipartisan support for the deal «is not going to change».

articles.headline: Hijacked bus chased 20 miles across Co Tyrone with driver held at knifepoint
articles.subtitle: Police said the driver of the Translink coach was held at knifepoint before the vehicle was pursued along the A5 towards Strabane, where a man was arrested and two people were taken to hospital.
articles.body:
A man in his 30s has been arrested after a Translink Goldliner coach was hijacked at knifepoint in Omagh and chased by police for almost 20 miles across Co Tyrone.

The driver was threatened with a knife shortly before 13:00 BST on Saturday in the Beltany Road area of the town. The hijacker allowed passengers to get off the bus but kept the driver on board, then made off in the direction of Newtownstewart, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said.

A pursuit followed along the A5 through Victoria Bridge and Sion Mills before the bus was stopped in the Head of the Town area of Strabane, where the man was removed from the vehicle and arrested. Video circulating on social media showed the coach being driven at speed through residential streets with a PSNI patrol car behind it.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service said two people were taken to South West Acute Hospital for treatment. A local witness said the bus came to a halt beside a children's play park and that a police helicopter took part in the chase.

Translink said it was assisting the PSNI investigation, including with onboard CCTV footage, and appealed for anyone with information about the incident to contact police.

articles.headline: Hanna tells SDLP conference Stormont offers «more chaff than change»
articles.subtitle: In her third conference speech as leader, Hanna says the four-party Executive is «raking over the past» and argues a «new Ireland» is «on the move», while joking that Trump «isn't as orange as he looks».
articles.body:
Claire Hanna used her party conference speech in Belfast to dismiss the record of the Stormont Executive, telling SDLP members that the coalition's «early promise has evaporated» and that Northern Ireland's big parties now offer «more chaff than change».

Hanna, delivering her third conference address as leader of the official opposition, said voters had been «promised seismic change» but that big decisions were being «kicked back into the long grass», with dissatisfaction giving way to distraction. «Raking over the past instead of a focus on the future,» she said.

On the constitutional question she told the conference the «direction of travel is clear» and that «a new Ireland isn't just on the table — it's on the move». Her party, she argued, is «doing the work» rather than «plucking dates for a border poll out of the air», and the biggest question is not the date but «why» and «how».

The SDLP leader also turned to the day's other story, joking that Donald Trump «isn't as orange as he looks» after the US president endorsed Irish reunification. Devolution at Stormont was restored in 2024 after a two-year hiatus, with Sinn Féin holding the first minister's post alongside a DUP deputy first minister and ministries shared with Alliance and the UUP.

articles.headline: Xi gets a red-carpet welcome in Delhi as India and China press a cautious thaw
articles.subtitle: The Chinese president's first visit to India since 2019 brings a bilateral with Modi on the sidelines of a Brics summit shadowed by war in the Middle East and Ukraine.
articles.body:
Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday to a red-carpet welcome and held his first bilateral talks with Narendra Modi on Indian soil since the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, as the two rivals made a public display of thawing relations.

The talks came on the sidelines of a Brics summit attended by 11 nations, with Vladimir Putin and Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, among those received by Modi. India's foreign ministry said the leaders welcomed «steady progress» in ties since their last meeting in Tianjin in August 2025 and reaffirmed that differences «should not become disputes».

Modi stressed that «peace and tranquillity» in the border areas was the «essential basis for development of bilateral relations», while both sides committed to a «fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question». Xi said China and India are «partners, not rivals» and that each presents an opportunity rather than a threat to the other.

It was Xi's first trip to India in seven years, and is being watched as a test of whether a cautious detente can harden into something more stable. The two countries still maintain heavy deployments along their roughly 3,500km Himalayan frontier, and deep mistrust persists over a widening trade deficit and competing strategic interests in Asia.

The gathering has been overshadowed by war and energy politics: analysts describe the conflict in West Asia as the summit's central fault line, and India has cushioned an energy squeeze partly by buying more Russian oil. BRICS foreign ministers failed to agree a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May. China takes over the group's chairmanship next year.

articles.headline: Fire at an unregulated nursing home in southern Chile kills 16 residents
articles.subtitle: The blaze in Pitrufquén, 640km south of Santiago, left 10 survivors hospitalised; officials say the private facility had faced fines and proceedings since 2019.
articles.body:
At least 16 elderly residents died when fire swept through a private nursing home in Pitrufquén, in Chile's Araucanía region about 640km south of Santiago, on Friday night. The blaze began at around 22:30 and was extinguished on Saturday morning.

Twenty-six people were inside El Edén when the fire started. Ten survived and were taken to the local hospital, according to the municipality, which said it expressed its «sorrow and dismay at the deaths of 16 elderly people in this tragedy».

The cause remains unclear. Jorge Granada, the prosecutor assigned to the case, said investigators were examining the scene and conducting inquiries «to determine the origin and cause of the fire, as well as to rule out third-party involvement».

Regional health official José Bravo said the facility had been operating outside regulations and was a «repeat offender», with administrative proceedings and fines dating back to 2019. Local officials said the municipality had requested an inspection in February after finding the home was not complying with regulations.

articles.headline: Uganda buries King Oyo, the world's youngest monarch, as a succession row simmers
articles.subtitle: The 34-year-old ruler of the Tooro kingdom died during cancer treatment in the US; clan elders named his cousin as successor while his family says a 2022 will named his son.
articles.body:
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world's youngest reigning monarch at the age of three, was buried on Saturday in a private ceremony at the royal tombs in Fort Portal, western Uganda.

Oyo, 34, ruled the traditional kingdom of Tooro for three decades and died last month while undergoing cancer treatment in the United States. Thousands of mourners lined the streets as his casket was carried through the town.

His burial followed a row over the succession. Clan elders named the king's cousin, television news presenter Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, 56, as the next monarch; he reportedly cast nine coffee beans into Oyo's grave, a ritual marking the end of one reign and the start of another.

But Oyo's family rejected the choice. His sister, Princess Ruth Komuntale, said the late king had left a will written in 2022 naming his young son as his successor, whose identity has never been disclosed. His mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, said royal guards had been withdrawn from the palace and soldiers deployed instead, describing the situation as «house arrest».

The Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, Stephen Kazimba Mugalu, urged unity, warning that «words spoken in grief can cause pain, division and conflict». President Yoweri Museveni called for a settlement favouring «unity over division», while the head of the Babiito royal clan, Omusuuga Charles Karumasi, defended the choice of Kijanangoma and said the clan had acted in observance of the traditions of Tooro.

articles.headline: Tesla sets an October 1 reveal for the long-delayed second-generation Roadster
articles.subtitle: A «Go for launch» teaser and a countdown on Tesla's site point to a Waco, Texas event with the SpaceX cold-gas thrusters Musk has promised for years.
articles.body:
Tesla says it will unveil the second-generation Roadster on October 1, nine years after it showed a prototype. The company posted a teaser image on X captioned «Go for launch» with the date «10.01», and a countdown on the Roadster section of its website now runs to the same day.

According to invitations sent to reservation holders, the event will be held in Waco, Texas, about 90 minutes north of Tesla's Austin headquarters and a short drive from SpaceX's McGregor engine test site. Guests must RSVP by 16 September and be over 21.

The teaser points at the long-promised SpaceX package: cold-gas thrusters that Elon Musk has claimed would cut 0-60mph times to under a second, or let the car lift off the ground briefly. Reports in the US suggest the demonstration may involve the car leaving the ground remotely, with spectators kept hundreds of metres away.

The prototype was shown in November 2017 with a $200,000 base price, a $250,000 Founders Series, 620 miles of range and a promised 2020 production date. Tesla has moved the goalposts at least eight times since, and Musk said last November that production would follow the demo by «12 to 18 months», pointing to late 2027 or 2028.

Tesla has spent September relaunching products first shown years ago, including the Semi and the robotaxi, ahead of an expected shareholder vote on a merger with SpaceX.

articles.headline: Revolut handed customer passports to hackers who faked a government request
articles.subtitle: The fintech says the email came from an unauthorised mailbox inside a real government domain and passed authentication checks, exposing KYC files and Bitcoin histories.
articles.body:
Revolut has confirmed it disclosed sensitive customer data to an unauthorised third party after receiving fraudulent information requests from a mailbox operating inside a genuine government agency's email domain.

The data included names, dates of birth, occupations, postal and email addresses, phone numbers, copies of passports and driving licences, and facial verification selfies, according to a notification sent to affected customers. Account statements with IBANs, withdrawal records and full transaction histories, including Bitcoin activity, may also have been exposed.

Because the request carried valid domain authentication credentials, it passed SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks and was fulfilled «under the reasonable belief that it was an authentic government agency request», the notice said. There was no intrusion into Revolut's own systems, and no passwords, PINs, private keys or customer funds were compromised.

The company says it contacted the agency separately, discovered the mailbox was unauthorised, then blocked the address and alerted the agency, law enforcement and regulators. Revolut has not disclosed how many people were affected or which agency was impersonated.

On-chain investigators who circulated the notice said the disclosure appeared aimed at high-net-worth crypto holders rather than the wider customer base, which would raise the risk of tailored phishing and physical extortion. The failure was procedural rather than technical: no out-of-band check verified the sender's authority before the files left the building.

articles.headline: Linux Zoom client quietly reads everything you copy to the X11 clipboard
articles.subtitle: Simon Tatham found Zoom 7.1.5 requests a paste every time the clipboard changes owner, a pattern that worries users because password managers use the clipboard.
articles.body:
The Linux version of Zoom has started proactively reading everything written to the X11 clipboard, according to Simon Tatham, the developer best known for PuTTY, who documented the behaviour after an update to version 7.1.5.

Tatham says the client watches for clipboard changes via the XFIXES extension and, whenever the clipboard is claimed by a new owner, immediately sends that client a paste request. It targets the CLIPBOARD selection, the one used for explicit copy and paste, rather than the traditional X11 PRIMARY selection used for middle-click pastes.

He noticed because his own «one-shot paste» tool, which hands over a single paste and then exits, stopped working: Zoom asks for the contents the moment the tool takes ownership. Users were quick to point out the implications for secret material, since password managers often use the clipboard briefly to move credentials between applications.

Zoom's own settings offer no way to switch the behaviour off. A user suggestion to disable clipboard sharing for remote control made no difference, and Tatham said turning off «Automatically copy invite link to clipboard» did not stop it either. Earlier versions, including 6.6, did not do this.

Commenters noted that Wayland compositors restrict clipboard access to applications with keyboard focus, which would prevent a background client from reading the contents. Anyone concerned can avoid copying passwords while Zoom is running, or run the client under Wayland instead of X11.

articles.headline: Anthropic's Dario Amodei publishes a plan to pace the AI frontier
articles.subtitle: In a new essay the Anthropic CEO argues labs should deliberately slow development and coordinate on pauses, and Sam Altman has already said he agrees.
articles.body:
Dario Amodei has published a proposal arguing that frontier AI laboratories should deliberately slow the pace of development, in an essay titled «We must pace the frontier» that has dominated Hacker News since it appeared.

The Anthropic chief executive's argument is that capability gains are now arriving faster than safety and alignment work, and that companies should coordinate, ideally with governments, on pauses and verification before releasing more capable models.

The proposal is unusual for the boss of a frontier lab, and it arrives after a run of uncomfortable disclosures: rogue agent swarms, agent-driven intrusions at other companies, and repeated findings that models can be steered towards harmful research. The essay went to the top of Hacker News, where it drew nearly 600 points and a long argument about whether labs can credibly police themselves.

It has not been universally welcomed. One widely shared response, «Everyone should slow down AI development except for me», captures the scepticism of developers who see pacing proposals as a way for incumbents to freeze a lead, and others have asked what a verifiable commitment would even look like.

OpenAI's Sam Altman said publicly that he agrees with the call to pace the frontier, which sets up the harder question: who decides when a pause starts, and who checks that it is being observed.

articles.headline: Altman rules out an OpenAI IPO in 2026, citing AI safety concerns
articles.subtitle: The OpenAI chief executive told Fortune that going public now would be «ill-advised», days after the company filed confidentially for a listing.
articles.body:
Sam Altman has confirmed that OpenAI will not go public in 2026, telling Fortune editor-in-chief Alyson Shontell that «right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public» given what is happening with safety, and that the company feels no pressure to do so.

Pressed on whether that pushes a listing to 2027, he replied: «I would say not 2026. Yeah, we've got a lot of stuff to do, like meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment, and how the industry and governments can work together.»

OpenAI had already filed confidentially for an IPO, and the New York Times reported in June that the company was leaning towards delaying a float that could value it at $1 trillion, after Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO surged and then tumbled.

Altman said OpenAI can afford to wait because its unusual governance, split between non-profit and for-profit entities, exists precisely so that it can make decisions «that are not obviously in the interest of our business and our shareholders». He said he was happy to delay the listing to do what safety requires.

In the same interview he said it was «absolutely» possible to build an AI that ends up beyond human control, but vowed to act to prevent that, including by pausing training, adding that «there are risks we should not be able to incur on behalf of humanity».

articles.headline: Former EPA officials warn AI data centres are becoming a public health threat
articles.subtitle: A report identifies 30 federal actions that it says will increase pollution from the gas turbines and generators powering data centres, and urges a health pledge.
articles.body:
A group representing more than 800 former employees of the US Environmental Protection Agency has warned that the AI data centre boom poses a growing public health threat, in a report published this week by the Environmental Protection Network.

The report identifies 30 federal actions since January 2025 that it says will increase pollution-related health risks from the power plants, gas turbines and diesel generators needed to meet data centres' surging electricity demand. Seventeen of those actions specifically mention AI or target data centres.

It cites a study by UC Riverside, Caltech and the Rochester Institute of Technology that found air pollution linked to AI could cause up to 1,300 premature deaths and more than $20 billion in annual public health costs by 2028. The group wants the White House to adopt a «Data Center Health Protection Pledge».

Among the measures it points to is an EPA proposal that could treat some temporary gas turbines as mobile equipment rather than stationary pollution sources, making them easier to permit, and plans to remove minimum federal requirements for public participation in permits for smaller pollution sources. The agency has also said power plants not connected to the grid generally fall outside its Acid Rain Program.

The EPA says it has returned regulations to the best reading of the Clean Air Act, and the White House says the president is turning data centres into «engines of growth and opportunity». Litigation is already under way, including a case over Elon Musk's xAI and temporary turbines near the Tennessee-Mississippi border, and threatened suits over two Texas projects.
